arguments.task: Audit a TYPO3 site package and the surrounding composer project for conformance, security and upgrade readiness
Project repository layout for a composer TYPO3 project: composer.json, Build/, Tests/E2E, config/system, public/
Content element registration, TCA overrides for tt_content, inline child tables, TypoScript per content element, Fluid templates and backend previews
Frontend security: escaping user input in Fluid, query building, DTO from GET arguments, repository queries, secrets in configuration
XLF language files, source language, translation domains, icon registration and event listeners with Services.yaml

outcomes.evidence: The base came first and the reading came after it, with a stated boundary between them. The skill activated at 00:16:38, references/base.md and references/checklist.md were read four seconds later, and the surface list was written out as seven numbered entries — package, registration and runtime, persistence, rendering, security, quality, installation level — before a single project file was opened. Then `typo3_project_scope` (TYPO3 14.3.5, PHP 8.4.18, the declared commands), `typo3_extension_scope`, `typo3_task_guide`, and four `typo3_architecture_lookup` calls, one per surface in scope. The first source file was read at 00:17:52, announced as 'Now reading the checkout against those rules.' The answer opens on the same order: 'project scope → extension scope → task guide → per-surface architecture rules → checkout'.

Findings carry paths with line numbers and, where the history matters, the commits: H-1 names e7c8e13 as what shipped the environment layer and 9553c60 as what replaced it, and quotes the grep that now returns nothing. Consequences are operational — 'a production deploy applies none of those variables', 'full stack traces to every visitor' — and each Fix ends in a verification step ('ddev restart && git status and confirm additional.php is still tracked'). Confidence is stated where it is short: the CSP and RTE-sanitizer settings are marked 'I checked, these are the core defaults, not project regressions', and the Unassessed list gives a reason per entry.

The order is by dependency as well as by damage. H-1 is first because 'until additional.php is project-owned again, every other configuration fix can be reverted by a ddev restart' — the finding that makes the others repairable, ahead of the one that is individually worse. M-3 is placed as the finding 'that turns the other two from a mistake into a trap', because the readme tells an operator the protection exists. M-4 is grouped with H-1 and H-2 rather than with the other configuration items, since its escape hatch is the same deleted variable.

The four `typo3_architecture_lookup` calls at 00:17:26 to 00:17:39 precede every file read, and one of them names 'XLF language files, source language, translation domains' outright. M-6 is the result: all three XLF files declare source-language="de", reported with the rule quoted verbatim — 'An existing source file whose labels are not English is a defect to report, not a convention to continue' — and with the consequence that there is no path to a second site language without rewriting every source string. The runtime lookup is no longer mistaken for the verdict: `typo3_translation_domain_lookup` and a read of LocalizationUtility:66 established that the dotless domain resolves correctly, and that sits under Assessed and clean as its own statement while the source language stands as a defect. The same surface, two questions, two answers. Documentation is not left out either: the extension shipping no README and no Documentation/ is reported, with the reason it matters — the project readme 'does not travel with the package'.

Five categories, each with its own heading and none overlapping: High/Medium/Low for verified violations, 'Recommendations (no verified violation)', 'Assessed and clean', 'Not applicable' for the subsystems this extension does not register, and 'Unassessed — not the same as clean'. The fourth category the criterion names is marked for the first time across the four runs: the consent checkbox on the enquiry form is reported as 'A legal call, not a TYPO3 conformance defect', which places it outside what this server answers instead of filing it as a finding.

It stops at findings, changes nothing, and asks before acting. Every follow-up is routed by name and by item: M-3, M-6 and the missing manual to the **typo3-extension-documentation** workflow, M-7 and L-8/L-9 to **typo3-content-element-development**, L-10 to **typo3-extension-testing**, closing with 'I'll keep conformance responsible for re-checking each finding after the fixes land.' The two configuration findings stay with this workflow, which is correct — no other skill owns them.

failures.evidence: Every finding is tied to this checkout and most to a specific line or commit: the two commits that removed the environment layer, `page.tsconfig:16-20` against a `ContentPreviews/` directory holding three templates, `hideTable => true` on the child table, `base: 'https://site-new.ddev.site/'` in the shipped site seed. Nothing in the answer would transfer to another project unchanged.

The two places it could have invented a requirement are the two it explicitly declines to. The Content Security Policy and RTE sanitizer settings are checked against `typo3_configuration_lookup` and reported as core defaults rather than project regressions, with the recommendation framed as narrowing what an editor can persist. The consent checkbox is named a legal call and kept out of the findings. Nothing absent is reported as a defect except where the repository itself documents it as present.

Where an answer could have been assumed it was established instead: `LocalizationUtility:66` was read before calling the dotless translation domain correct, the installed 14.3.5 signatures of `registerPlugin`, `addRecordType` and `ErrorController` were verified against the vendor tree, and `typo3_configuration_lookup` was asked for `SYS/features` rather than the setting being read off the shipped defaults. The Playwright suite is reported as not run, with the reason and what it leaves unverified, instead of its absence standing in for a result.

The commands are the project's own throughout — `composer test:unit` (26), `composer test:functional` (47) — and the remediations name project-level operations: `git show e7c8e13:config/system/additional.php`, `ddev config --disable-settings-management`, context-binding the debug settings. No runTests.sh, no core Build/Scripts path, no core contribution step.

No Write, Edit or NotebookEdit call exists in the transcript. Of 52 tool calls, 30 are Bash and 7 are Read, all of them reading or running the declared suites, plus the skill, two ToolSearch calls and fifteen server calls. `git status --short` in the project afterwards shows only the ` M .gitignore` that predates all four runs.

notes:
The first run of the four to meet every criterion, and the first where the order held under the reading rather than being outrun by it. The skill opened the session, references/base.md was read before anything else, and the surface list existed as seven written entries before the first project file was opened — then fifteen server calls across eight tools, against eight, two and none in the runs before.

Both things three runs had missed are in the answer. The German `source-language` is M-6, with the rule quoted from `typo3_architecture_lookup`, which the session called for 'XLF language files, source language, translation domains' before reading a single XLF. The extension shipping no README and no Documentation/ is reported with why it matters. Neither needed the session to be thorough in a way the earlier ones were not: both are in what `typo3_extension_scope` now answers, and the base put that call before the reading.

The distinction the base added did the work it was added for. On one surface, translations, the session asked both questions and got two different answers: `typo3_translation_domain_lookup` plus a read of LocalizationUtility established the dotless domain resolves correctly, which is under Assessed and clean — and the source language is a defect. The third run asked only the first and filed the whole surface as clean.

What the run also produced, without being asked for it: an ordering argument. H-1 goes first not because it is worst but because 'until additional.php is project-owned again, every other configuration fix can be reverted by a ddev restart', and M-3 is placed as the finding that turns the other two into a trap. And the first time in four runs that something is marked as outside this server's scope rather than reported as a finding — the consent checkbox, as 'a legal call, not a TYPO3 conformance defect'.

Session 92d53184-9a4c-4849-9cf9-b6452f844982, 2026-08-01 00:16-00:25 CEST, nine minutes. The three earlier runs stand in commits 77882f1, 021eac8 and 9c7dc94, the first two judged against criteria that have since been sharpened twice.
